title: Surface / Stadium Effects
hypothesis: Certain teams perform materially differently on grass vs. turf, dome vs. outdoor, after controlling for pregame team strength.
design: Team-level surface performance residual with heavy shrinkage (K=32-64). Test grass/turf split, dome/outdoor split.
notes: Likely confounded with home-field advantage and travel effects already in the model. Noted in EXP-027 research queue section.

title: Opponent-Adjusted Recent Form
hypothesis: Opponent-adjusting the current-season form component (W/L + point differential) improves prediction beyond raw form.
data_source: games.csv for results; v2.2 Elo for opponent strength.
design: Replace raw current-season form with SRS-style opponent-adjusted form. Distinct from EXP-006 (rejected) because it adjusts the form component itself, not just adding standalone SRS.
notes: The distinction from EXP-006 is subtle but meaningful. Noted in EXP-027 research queue section.

title: Market-Calibrated Meta-Stacker
hypothesis: L2 logistic regression combining v2.2 control, market no-vig, SRS, rest, travel, dome, and interaction terms beats market-only.
data_source: games.csv (moneylines, scores, surface, roof), v2.2 predictWinner, stadiumCoordinates
design: L2-regularized logistic meta-stacker with Platt scaling. 3 variants (18/6/3 features). Train 2022-2023, select 2024, confirm 2025, observe 2026 W1-3.
notes: REJECT FOR PROMOTION. 2025: 61.99% vs 66.42% control. 2026 W1-3: 62.50% vs 66.67% market. Calibration improved (ECE 0.0805 vs 0.1041). Miss patterns: home bias (72% away wins), market agreement (67%), Week 2 collapse (43.8%), dome weakness (46.7%). See research/EXP-030_MARKET_CALIBRATED_META_STACKER.md.

title: Gradient Boosted Trees Meta-Stacker
hypothesis: GBDT (XGBoost/LightGBM) captures non-linear feature interactions that logistic regression misses, improving winner accuracy.
data_source: Same features as EXP-030 plus play-by-play EPA from nflverse
design: GBDT meta-stacker with walk-forward validation. Requires adding ML package to repo. Address home bias with away-upset detection features.
notes: EXP-030 showed logistic regression overfits. GBDT may capture dome/Week 2 interactions better. Must address home bias problem first.

title: Away-Team Upset Detection Model
hypothesis: A model trained specifically on disagreement cases (where control and market disagree) can identify away-team upsets that the main model misses.
design: Train on disagreement cases only. Features: SRS diff, travel, rest, divisional, dome, spread distance, recent form differential.
notes: EXP-030 found 72% of misses were away wins and 67% agreed with market. Targeted upset detection could break this pattern.
